item.title: UK police arrest British national linked to airbase incident
item.description: 22-year old British national arrested on suspicion of a terror offence after other suspects released on bail.

item.title: Demonstrators clash with riot police in France as education protests mount
item.description: School blockades and clashes intensify in France as frustration rises over government education policy.

item.title: Former German spy chief arrested on suspicion of treason and espionage
item.description: August Hanning's former chief of staff was also arrested on suspicion of 'aiding and abetting attempted treason'.

item.title: Ukraine launches major drone attack on Russia’s Moscow region, killing two
item.description: Russia says 290 drones targeted Moscow and nearby regions in the overnight Ukrainian assault.

item.title: Francis Halzen wins Nobel Prize in Physics for work on ‘ghost particles’
item.description: Belgian physicist worked to build Antarctic observatory that tracks neutrinos from deep space.

item.title: Mapping where US bombers are based globally
item.description: The US has pulled its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford amid Iran fears. Here's where else they can fly from.

item.title: Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi deterrence against Houthis: What that means
item.description: Islamabad says its role is defensive, but Riyadh's offensive in Yemen tests how long it can stay out of the fight.

item.title: Qatar and India among seven countries bidding for 2036 Olympics, IOC says
item.description: South Africa, Turkiye, Germany, Hungary and South Korea are on the list of countries revealed by the IOC.

item.title: France’s student protests grow as hundreds of schools close
item.description: Al Jazeera’s Bernard Smith reports from France on the growing student protests across the country.

item.title: Tennis: World number one Sinner will not play in 2026 due to knee injury
item.description: Jannik Sinner has not competed in a tournament since winning at Wimbledon in July and will continue his recovery.

item.title: How Palestinian reporters defied Israel’s genocide to redefine journalism
item.description: Western media under scrutiny for promoting Israeli narrative rather than standing up for vulnerable journalists in Gaza.

item.title: Russia plague quarantine following lab death: Should we be worried?
item.description: Plague is still endemic to Siberia, the location of the first known prehistoric human outbreak.

item.title: India opposition leaders briefly arrested in protest against election chief
item.description: Protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

item.title: Pro-Palestine Greens challenge Labour’s grip on Starmer’s former seat
item.description: Green Party leader Zack Polanski hopes to shake Labour, which has held Holborn since the seat was created in 1983.

item.title: Singapore refers eight civil servants to police over property purchases
item.description: Minister announces referrals after think tank paper finds link between purchases and unannounced MRT stations.

item.title: Saudi Arabia says three wounded in attacks on airports near Yemen border
item.description: Saudi aviation authority reports severe injuries and damage following Houthi strikes on Jazan and Najran airports.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter to be executed by firing squad: All to know
item.description: The US Army is averse to capital punishment and has not carried out an execution in decades.

item.title: UEFA to investigate spitting incident at Ireland-Israel football match
item.description: An Israeli player is accused of spitting on an Irish coach as the teams returned to their dressing rooms at half-time.

item.title: Kenya ministry of health confirms first imported Ebola case
item.description: The first imported case of Ebola has been recorded in Kenya.

item.title: India’s ‘million mutinies’ are puncturing Modi’s aura of invincibility
item.description: Across the country, Indians are turning disparate grievances into a broader reckoning with unaccountable power.

item.title: ‘Hitting the right nail’: Refugee rescue group defiant as Greece targets it
item.description: Aegean Boat Report founder Tommy Olsen insists he is defending the rule of law, as Greece opens trial against him.

item.title: Palestine weekly: Olive harvest opens under assault
item.description: Israeli settlers and forces beat Palestinians, set property on fire and steal crops across the occupied West Bank.

item.title: South Korea considers steps to force North Korea apology for DMZ mine blast
item.description: Seoul has urged Pyongyang to remove any other mines planted on the southern side of the military demarcation line.

item.title: Malaysia’s Anwar to host Myanmar leader as repatriations near 10,000
item.description: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing to visit Kuala Lumpur 'in the next few days', Anwar Ibrahim says.

item.title: Gaza woman rescues books from rubble to keep education alive
item.description: Amid the destruction of Gaza’s schools and universities, Niveen Al-Gharabli has built a makeshift book stall.
